# Nigerian mobile-number detection

<!-- Generated by node ci/rule-packs/build-detection.mjs --write. -->

Finds contiguous national mobile numbers with the existing prefix validator and international 234 or +234 numbers with exact prefix alternatives. Both rules report error findings. Prefixes are pack data.

Version: `2026.11.0`. Source: `rule-packs/phone.pack.json`.

The citation register records owner approval in principle; legal review remains pending. A finding requests review and does not establish a legal breach.

| Rule | Severity | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| `pii.phone` | error | Review protection of identifying telephone numbers. Sections 24(1)(c), 24(1)(f), 39 and 65; Article 29(1)-(2). |
| `pii.phone.international` | error | Review protection of identifying telephone numbers. Sections 24(1)(c), 24(1)(f), 39 and 65; Article 29(1)-(2). |

## Limits

The prefix snapshot is the NCC March 2024 numbering plan, reviewed on 6 November 2026. It covers full mobile blocks for Airtel, EMTS, Glo and MTN, including the former Visafone 704 block. It excludes fixed lines, shared-service blocks and partial 702 allocations. It is a pinned baseline, not a claim of exhaustive 2026 allocation coverage. Spaces, hyphens and parentheses inside a number are not supported. Prefixes do not establish assignment, current carrier, processing purpose or an unlawful disclosure. International alternatives include the plus sign in the finding span when present; the digits-only validator cannot validate that sign, so these alternatives encode the same prefix data in the shape.

## Remediation and exceptions

Replace unnecessary telephone data in source and fixtures with generated data; mask values before logging or returning them. Record a narrowly scoped justified exception where retention is necessary.

## Verification

Run `dotnet test tests/Corpus.Tests -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~DetectionPackTests` for exact locations and measured synthetic precision/recall.

These are unsigned release-source packs. Tests sign only in memory with the labelled development key. Production signing, embedding and publication are separate release operations; no development signature is shipped.
